summary: Set 131 Session 3 of 3, 'Rotation, the lever that was never written down' - the SET-TERMINAL session. Sessions 1 and 2 changed policy and code; this one is documentation and three pointer files, with a spec-declared irony budget of ZERO new test functions, and it delivered exactly that: pytest closed at 4490 passed / 9 skipped, the same count as Session 2. SHIPPED: a new canonical section in docs/ai-led-session-workflow.md, 'Rotation, and the trade we declined', placed between Delegation Discipline and the decision-rights rubric. It records the largest measured cost effect in this repo's history - conversation a9f211a7 (1,148 inferences, $367.18) compacted at turn 75, input fell 631,304 -> 54,119 tokens and cost fell ~33-35 -> ~3.6-5.0 credits per inference, a ~7-8x reduction for a one-time 400 credits with payback in ~14 inferences - together with the banded evidence that it is not one conversation's accident (7.65 credits/inference at 25-75K, 9.76 at 75-150K, 17.18 at 150-300K, 35.77 above 300K on the same model). THE THRESHOLD IS THIS SESSION'S OWN DECISION, journaled: the spec demanded 'a token threshold, not a vibe' and named no number. Rotate at ~150K retained input, at the first step boundary after the threshold is crossed - 150K because that is where the measured curve leaves its plateau, and a step boundary because a boundary already produces most of the carry-forward a flush needs, so rotating there is cheaper than rotating mid-step. Alternatives (300K, 600K, no number) are in decisions.jsonl with their consequences. The section also ships a SURVIVAL CONTRACT naming what must live through a flush (bootstrap file, spec and active step, session-state.json, activity log, open findings with severities, and a dense record of what was tried and rejected and why) and what must not be assumed to survive (anything discovered only in the transcript), plus the failure mode: a rotated session repeats a path it already abandoned. That is the same premise as Delegation Discipline rule 3's statefulness carve-out, because a post-rotation orchestrator is a delegate to its own earlier self, and the two sections now cite each other in both directions as the spec required. Rotation stays MANUAL - an automatic trigger is an explicit spec non-goal, on the reasoning that a writer which flushes an orchestrator's transcript on its behalf should not ship in the set that first measured the effect. THE DECLINED TRADE is on the record with its evidence: the naive per-model table (opus-5 22.40 credits/inference, sonnet-4.6 4.51, gemini-3.1-pro 2.65) is reproduced DELIBERATELY, immediately above the matched-context table that refutes it, so a future reader who rediscovers the naive numbers finds them already labelled as role/context confounding rather than re-deriving an 8.5x conclusion. At matched context claude-opus-5 and gpt-5.5 cost the same per inference across three consecutive bands despite multipliers of 15.0 and 7.5. The substitution lever is ~1.7-2x; the rotation lever on the SAME model is 4.7x. Downgrading the only actor holding write, shell and network rights is a confused-deputy risk the children's read-only allowlist does not close, so the trade is declined and the reasoning is written where an orchestrator reads it. L-064-8 THREE-SURFACE DRIFT, FIXED: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md are supposed to differ only in their engine-specific bootstrap. CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md still named 'Set 110 Session 4 and Sets 111-112' as a LIVE window, AGENTS.md had drifted to a compressed variant of the same stale claim, and all three pointed readers at 'human-tunable thresholds' that Session 1 had just deleted as phantom keys. The Delegation Discipline pointer is now byte-identical in all three - verified mechanically, 1,129 bytes and the same SHA-256 in each. docs/planning/orchestration-strategy.md gained rotation as a fourth cost lever beside its three currencies, pointing at the canonical section rather than restating it. VERIFICATION: round 1 (discovery, 2-way fan-out, both calls gpt-5.5, anthropic excluded as the orchestrator's effective provider by registry lookup) returned VERIFIED with 0 blocking findings and one Nit per lens. Under this repo's loop discipline a Minor-only round is effectively VERIFIED and the nits could simply have been recorded. Both were fixed instead: (1) the 150-300K payback was stated as 'inside ~30' when the section's own savings range gives 31-33, or ~42 if the post-flush context settles at the 25-75K band average - an optimistic rounding inside a paragraph headed 'Payback, stated honestly', now a stated range with both endpoints attributed; (2) the matched-context table carried two models where the spec's source table carries four, which mattered because the naive table's CHEAPEST rows are gemini-3.1-pro and sonnet-4.6 - exactly the rows a reader would reach for - so the table now reproduces all four models and all five bands with each cell's n, plus a paragraph naming what the empty cells mean (the two cheap-looking models have no data above 150K because nothing ever asked them to hold an orchestrator's context, which is trap T1 restated where a reader meets the evidence). post_round_delta classified that delta as shipped-code (A4.2) because docs/ai-led-session-workflow.md sits outside every declared test surface, so round 2 ran as the obligation names: one delta-scoped remediation-review against the round-1 baseline tree, gpt-5.5 with anthropic excluded, carrying a conventions block naming both edits and nothing else. VERIFIED, 0 findings. Running it here rather than meeting it inside close_session costs the same money and is the only version in which its findings could have been acted on. TEST COMPOSITION (project-guidance requires this be stated, not presented as one clean run): pytest 4490 passed / 9 skipped in one invocation (753s); mocha 1455 passing / 2 pending in one invocation (42s); playwright 30 passed in the declared invocation (7.4m) with vsix-first-run-walkthrough.spec.ts:218 timing out at 300s waiting for the scaffold to write two lifecycle sets, then that one spec re-run in isolation and passing in 45.3s - 6.6x inside the budget it had just exhausted. That is the THIRD consecutive session of this set to hit the identical spec for the identical load-induced reason (S1 57.6s, S2 56.6s, S3 45.3s); the route is journaled in decisions.jsonl, and three recurrences inside one set are now a recorded artifact for whichever set decides to fix the spec's fixture wait. Every test in all three suites executed and passed. STEP 3.5: the next-session-set recommendation was routed, not self-opined - gpt-5.5 with anthropic excluded, the router's own verify pass gemini-3.1-pro-preview returning VERIFIED with 0 issues, saved raw as s3-next-set-routed.md. It recommends running the already-authored Set 132 next rather than authoring a competing set, with delegation telemetry second - the new policy claims its reason codes are 'audited in aggregate' and no data source for that audit exists yet. SET CLOSES HERE. change-log.md and the single ai_router/changelog.d fragment cover all three sessions, including Session 2's rename of premium_request_weight to probe_premium_requests, which Session 2's disposition put this session on notice to record.
